title: Sema — From Human Intent to Verified AI Execution

scenes.headline: Speed without memory becomes drift.
scenes.narration: AI agents can change code in seconds. But a real project is more than code: it carries intent, rules, and promises. When those disappear between tasks, speed becomes drift.

scenes.headline: Stop rescanning. Start from the map.
scenes.narration: You tell Codex what you want. Instead of scanning the whole project from scratch on every task, Codex consults Sema for the context that matters, then works from a precise semantic map.

scenes.headline: One bootstrap. A permanent protocol.
scenes.narration: On first contact, the real bootstrap runs in a small payments project with no Sema and no AGENTS.md. It checks the local CLI, creates the first living contract, and generates its AGENTS.md, the permanent handshake future Codex tasks read automatically.

scenes.headline: The contract points Codex to the code.
scenes.narration: The living contract preserves your intent, rules, guarantees, and semantic links, leading Codex directly to the relevant code. Codex implements the request. Sema then verifies that implementation against the contract.

scenes.headline: Rename the symbol. Preserve the promise.
scenes.narration: The task is concrete: complete a payment approval rename from approvePayment to confirmPayment without losing the receipt guarantee. A partial rename already exists in the code, while the semantic contract still points to the old symbol. It is a quiet mismatch that could poison the next change.

scenes.headline: No guesswork. No fake green check.
scenes.narration: Before editing, Codex asks Sema for context, required documentation, and drift. Sema resolves the contract against the implementation and stops the change: the old approvePayment link is broken. The result names the contract, the symbol, and the affected files. No guesswork, and no fake green check.

scenes.headline: Evidence defines done.
scenes.narration: Codex inspects the applicable dot-sema contract, maps the impact, then updates the contract and implementation together. The business promise remains explicit: every approved payment returns a receipt ID. Validation passes, the symbol link resolves, tests pass, and drift returns green. Only then does Sema close the change with its required documentation recorded as evidence.

scenes.headline: Sema governs its own development.
scenes.narration: I use Sema entirely through Codex. Build Week made me stop building a separate OpenCode-based IDE and stop spreading Sema across every assistant. With GPT-5.6 through Codex, I made the CLI the engine, AGENTS.md the handshake, and the plugin first contact—then verified the public package. Sema governs its own development.

scenes.headline: From human intent to verified AI execution.
scenes.narration: Software is the proving ground, not the boundary. The same chain—intent, context, contract, impact, execution, evidence—can govern any structured work performed by agents. Sema: from human intent to verified AI execution.
